hero.lead: A nation of 285.7 million across seventeen thousand islands, where nine in ten cook with clean fuel and the World Bank has committed more than $2.9 billion since 2025.

capital.heading: Indonesia finances at scale and pioneered the green sukuk. Next, safe water in every home.

record.text: The world’s first sovereign green sukuk, issued February 2018
Productive and Sustainable Investment DPL: Financial sector and renewable procurement
Sustainable Least-Cost Electrification-2 (ISLE-2): Power for 3.5 million people; 540 MW of solar and wind
Electricity Network Transformation (I-ENET): About $1.33 billion with PLN and private capital

register.name: Inaugural sovereign panda bonds
register.detail: Issued July 2026 · Onshore China bond market · The Republic’s first panda bonds
register.note: First sovereign borrowing in China’s onshore market
register.text: The Republic’s first bonds in renminbi, sold in China’s onshore market. They widen the investor base that finances the state budget.

register.name: Global Sukuk with a 30-year green tranche
register.detail: Priced 25 June 2024 · Settled 2 July 2024 · 5-year $750M at 5.10%, 10-year $1B at 5.20%, 30-year green $600M at 5.50%
register.text: Sharia-compliant bonds sold to global investors, with a 30-year green tranche for climate and environmental projects under the Republic’s green framework. Orders reached $4.5 billion, more than 1.9 times the issue.

register.name: Global Sukuk with a 30-year green tranche
register.detail: Priced 3 June 2021 · Settled 9 June 2021 · 5-year $1.25B at 1.50%, 10-year $1B at 2.55%, 30-year green $750M at 3.55%
register.text: Sharia-compliant bonds for the state budget, with a 30-year green tranche, the Republic’s fourth global green sukuk. Orders reached $10.3 billion, more than 3.4 times the issue.

register.name: Sovereign green sukuk, first issuance
register.note: The world’s first sovereign green sukuk
register.text: The world’s first sovereign green sukuk, for projects that mitigate or adapt to climate change and preserve biodiversity. Indonesia has since added green tranches to its global sukuk, among them in 2021 and 2024.

register.name: Local Service Delivery Improvement Project
register.detail: Approved 18 December 2025 · Starts with 30 local governments
register.note: Solid waste services for more than 15 million people
register.text: Strengthens solid waste services and infrastructure, starting with 30 local governments. It aims to give more than 15 million Indonesians cleaner surroundings and better protect 10 million from climate risks, for the shelter and health standards.

register.name: Electricity Network Transformation (I-ENET)
register.note: About $1.33 billion with PLN and private capital
register.text: Upgrades the Java, Madura and Bali grid for about 20 million people.

register.name: Productive and Sustainable Investment DPL
register.text: Removes obstacles to renewable energy and draws private capital into infrastructure.

register.name: Sustainable Least-Cost Electrification-2 (ISLE-2)
register.note: Power for 3.5 million people; 540 MW of solar and wind
register.text: Brings electricity to Kalimantan and Sumatra.

register.name: Financial Market Deepening Program, Subprogram 1
register.note: Capital markets, digital finance and transition finance
register.text: Supports deeper capital markets, safer digital financial services with stronger rules for digital assets and cybersecurity, and sustainable and transition finance. The first subprogram is backed by $650 million of ADB financing.

register.name: Solid Waste Management for Sustainable Urban Development Project
register.note: Waste treatment, landfill upgrades and circular-economy grants
register.text: AIIB financing for waste treatment facilities, landfill upgrades, institutional strengthening, community programmes and circular-economy grants.

register.name: Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: Approved 20 September 2024 · Policy-based loan · First of two subprograms
register.note: Reforms for the shift to clean power
register.text: Supports renewable energy regulation, stronger governance and finances in the energy sector, and a fair and inclusive transition toward Indonesia’s 2050 net-zero goal for power, for the energy standard.

register.name: Competitiveness, Industrial Modernization, and Trade Acceleration Program, Subprogram 2
register.note: Investment climate, trade logistics and local businesses
register.text: Supports investment-climate reforms, digital trade logistics and stronger local businesses, including women-owned enterprises, for livelihood.

register.name: Sustainability-linked loan to Mitra Plumbon Healthcare
register.detail: Signed 27 February 2026 · Up to Rp415 billion
register.text: An ADB loan to a private hospital group that runs seven hospitals in West Java, where more than 80% of patients are covered by national health insurance (JKN). It finances a new hospital in Batang, Central Java, and a new outpatient building in Cirebon, adding 350 beds, for the health standard.

register.name: Pasuruan 100 MW Solar PV Project
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2025 · Non-sovereign · Sponsors PLN Indonesia Power Renewables and Vena Energy Indonesia
register.note: 100 MW ground-mounted solar plant, East Java
register.text: AIIB financing for a 100 MW greenfield solar plant in Pasuruan, East Java, for the energy standard.

register.name: Cornerstone investment in the Medela Potentia IPO
register.text: IFC equity in an integrated pharmaceutical distributor that serves more than 3,000 hospitals, 23,000 pharmacies and 3,500 clinics in Indonesia and Cambodia, for the health standard.

register.name: Amartha asset-backed securities
register.detail: Approved 11 May 2023 · Invested 4 December 2023 · Up to $150M more sought from other investors
register.text: IFC investment in Amartha, one of Indonesia’s largest microfinance lenders, which lends through a peer-to-peer platform to women entrepreneurs; about 1.2 million borrowers in September 2022. It serves livelihood.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 59 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street market in Jakarta

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Green rice terraces in Bali, Indonesia

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest in Borneo, Indonesia, mist over the canopy

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A river winding through the rainforest of Kalimantan, Indonesia

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A geothermal power plant with steam rising in the hills of Java, Indonesia

items.name: Mitra Plumbon Healthcare
items.text: Runs seven hospitals in West Java with more than 2,700 beds; more than 80% of its patients are covered by national health insurance. It is adding 350 beds with an ADB loan.

items.name: Amartha
items.text: One of Indonesia’s largest microfinance lenders, lending through a peer-to-peer platform to women entrepreneurs: about 1.2 million borrowers in 2022.

coverage.gap_text: Indonesians without safely managed drinking water at home: 70 in every hundred.

guarantees.name: Shelter

guarantees.name: Energy

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 47.2% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school; 2015, dated

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$8.30 a day; 64.1% live below it
